scenes.title: Amputee looking at the vertical Mirror Box reflection as opening his intact right hand visually unclenches his left phantom spasm
scenes.era: 1995, UC San Diego Center for Brain and Cognition clinic room, La Jolla

layout.description: Sunlit 1995 UCSD neurology office with a clean wooden table holding Ramachandran's open-topped cardboard-and-wood Mirror Box divided down the center by a bright vertical glass mirror, creating the seamless optical illusion of two symmetrical open hands.

positions.who: Upper-Limb Amputee Participant (mannequin in rolled-sleeve collared shirt)
positions.where: seated at the wooden table placing his intact right hand in front of the vertical mirror while leaning slightly right so the reflection aligns cleanly where his missing left hand belongs
positions.facing: looking intently into the vertical mirror

positions.who: V. S. Ramachandran (mannequin in dark 1995 blazer and patterned tie)
positions.where: standing across the table pointing to the symmetrical reflected hand opening smoothly

props.name: vertical tabletop Mirror Box
props.period_detail: clean open-front rectangular box split by an upright frameless glass mirror
props.physical_behavior: superimposes the intact right hand's reflection precisely onto the missing left-hand coordinates

props.name: sterile cotton-tipped mapping swab & Penfield strip card
props.period_detail: resting beside the box from the cheek-to-thumb remapping exam

props.name: symmetrical open-palm reflection
props.period_detail: crystal-clear mirror image of five fingers stretching open smoothly
props.physical_behavior: delivers the missing 'movement succeeded!' visual return

actions.verb_sequence: places intact hand beside the vertical mirror in a tight fist matching his cramped phantom -> slowly stretches all five fingers wide open while watching the mirror reflection
points to the reflected 'left' hand opening cleanly in space

reactions.reaction: widens posture in astonishment and relief as the decade-long clenched phantom sensation releases
logs immediate phantom movement in 6 of 10 patients from a $10 mirror

scenes.wardrobe: 1995 San Diego academic/clinical dress: dark blazer, white shirt, and tie on Ramachandran; casual short-sleeve/rolled-cuff Oxford shirt on participant.
scenes.lighting: Bright, crisp California window daylight casting a clean, unmistakable reflection in the vertical mirror.
scenes.recognition_hook: His missing hand had felt frozen in a painful fist for years — until a $10 mirror propped in a box tricked his visual brain into watching 'both' hands stretch wide open.

key_visual.description: a 1995 neurology table with an open vertical Mirror Box reflecting a participant's intact open hand into the space of the missing hand while V. S. Ramachandran observes

scenes.title: Cotton swab on the cheek felt on the missing phantom thumb

layout.description: Bright clinical chair where a blindfolded participant raises a finger on his intact hand to report feeling a cheek cotton-swab stroke on his missing phantom thumb.

positions.where: brushing a clean cotton swab gently across the blindfolded patient's left cheek
pointing immediately to 'phantom thumb' on a hand chart

props.name: cotton swab & face-next-to-hand S1 diagram
props.period_detail: shows why cheek borders thumb on Penfield's strip

actions.verb_sequence: strokes three points on the cheek -> Patient maps distinct phantom fingers

scenes.recognition_hook: Because FACE sits right next to HAND on the brain's sensory strip, a cotton swab on the cheek lit up a missing thumb.

scenes.title: Modern 7-Tesla fMRI & daily stroke/phantom rehab protocol

layout.description: Sunlit physical therapy table where an occupational therapist guides a post-stroke patient through structured 20-minute daily folding-mirror-box hand exercises.

positions.where: practicing rhythmic finger taps in front of a folding tabletop mirror

props.name: modern folding therapy mirror & 4-week daily log
props.period_detail: shows clinical rigor beyond a one-time trick

actions.verb_sequence: completes daily 15-minute bilateral mirror routine checking off Week 3

scenes.wardrobe: Clean modern clinic polo and casual wear.
scenes.recognition_hook: Turned into a structured daily protocol, the $10 mirror moved from phantom limbs into mainstream stroke rehabilitation.

scenes.title: Using clean visual alignment during physical therapy stretching

layout.description: Bright studio wall mirror where watching smooth, symmetrical shoulder motion reduces protective muscle guarding.

positions.where: watching symmetrical slow arm lifts in a bright studio mirror with relaxed shoulders

props.name: full-clarity wall mirror
props.period_detail: confirms safe unthreatened range of motion

actions.verb_sequence: watches smooth symmetrical motion -> stiffness eases

scenes.recognition_hook: Seeing smooth, safe movement in real time helps your brain turn down protective motor guarding.
